in_greek.name: Φιδέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Φιδέλα προέρχεται από το λατινικό fidela, που σημαίνει πίστη και εὐπιστία, και είναι παράγωγο της λατινικής λέξης fides, που σημαίνει πίστη, και χρησιμεύει ως χριστιανικό όνομα για κορίτσι, που συμβολίζει την πίστη και την εὐπιστία που έχει κανείς στον Θεό

data.cultural_impact: The name Fidela holds historical significant as it has been used throughout history, especially during the medieval period, as a name for noblewomen and heroines in literature. These women were known for their unwavering loyalty and steadfastness, often making great personal sacrifices for their loved ones and their faith. They inspired subsequent generations with their strength and devotion, which helped to solidify the ideals of faithfulness and loyalty within European culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Fidela is a deeply spiritual name that reflects the Christian virtues of faithfulness, devotion, and unwavering commitment to God. The name emphasizes the importance of trusting in God's plan for our lives and remaining steadfast in our beliefs, even in the face of adversity. It calls to mind the story of the biblical character Ruth, who famously pledged her lifelong loyalty to Naomi, her mother-in-law, and Naomi's God, saying "where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay." (Ruth 1:16) This declaration of commitment and trustworthiness has resonated throughout history, inspiring countless men and women to live compassionate and faithful lives.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Spain, Fidela was a popular name for Christian girls during the Reconquista period, around the 11th to 13th centuries, when Christian forces were retaking territory from the Moors.
There is also a 3rd-century saint named Fidela, who was a virgin martyr in Sicily. She was tortured and beheaded, and her feast day is celebrated on January 21.
